issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping with no puddle, a sweet smell, white exhaust smoke, milky oil, overheating, or a misfire. Some owners see coolant seeping at the back corners of the intake.
issues.why: The 3.8L V6 uses plastic-framed intake manifold gaskets that break down and leak coolant, either outside or into the engine. Coolant mixed into the oil can wipe out the bearings. Consumer Guide lists this for 1993-1999.
issues.next: Check the coolant level often and look at the oil on the dipstick for a milky color. Fix it promptly; a gasket job is far smaller than replacing an engine. Change the oil after the repair.

issues.t: Plastic upper intake cracks and leaks coolant
issues.sym: Coolant leaking from the top of the engine, overheating, steam or smoke from under the hood, a misfire, or coolant and oil mixing. Some owners report the engine seizing afterward.
issues.why: The plastic upper intake plenum on the 3.8L has coolant passages that crack with heat and age. GM released an upgraded manifold, gaskets and PCV kit to correct coolant loss. NHTSA complaints for these years are dominated by intake failures.
issues.next: Stop driving if the temperature gauge climbs. Have the intake pressure-tested; replacing the upper intake with the updated part is the fix.

issues.t: Upper intake can break on a backfire at startup (recall)
issues.sym: A loud pop when starting, followed by a no-start, or a fire under the hood.
issues.why: A backfire while starting the 3.8L could crack the upper intake manifold. GM recalled the cars and reprogrammed the engine computer, and told owners to keep the hood shut while starting until it was done.
issues.next: If you hear a backfire and smell fuel or see smoke, turn the key off and get out. Ask a GM dealer whether the recall reprogramming was done.

issues.t: Leaking fuel pressure regulator can cause a backfire and fire (recall)
issues.sym: Hard starting, a fuel smell, a pop or backfire when cranking, or an engine fire.
issues.why: Some Delphi fuel pressure regulators on the 3.8L leaked fuel into the intake through a vacuum line. If the engine didn't start, the fuel could backfire, rupture the intake, loosen a fuel line and start a fire. GM installed improved regulators.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. If the engine cranks and won't start, don't keep cranking it. Have a GM dealer check that the regulator recall was done.

issues.t: Shift linkage clip can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: The gear shown on the indicator doesn't match the gear the car is in. It may move when you think it is in Park or Neutral.
issues.why: A clip linking the shifter to the transmission's manual valve could loosen and disconnect. GM replaced it with a spring-type fastener kit.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake. Have a GM dealer confirm the recall was done.

issues.t: Key-in-ignition and seat belt chimes may not work (recall)
issues.sym: No chime or light when you leave the key in or don't buckle up. Interior lights or power locks may act up.
issues.why: A body control module could have a damaged capacitor. GM inspected and replaced the module where needed.
issues.next: Ask a GM dealer whether the module recall was done.

issues.sym: At highway speed the engine revs up and the car loses drive, as if it shifted to neutral, even though the shifter shows Drive.
issues.why: Consumer Guide notes the 4T60-E automatic in these years can slip into neutral at highway speed because of internal shift valve problems. NHTSA owners describe the same thing.
issues.next: Coast to a safe stop and turn on your hazards. Have a transmission shop diagnose it before driving at speed again.

issues.sym: A long delay before reverse engages, no reverse at all, shudder on hard acceleration, or complete loss of drive.
issues.why: NHTSA complaints describe reverse failing or engaging late, sticking or leaking piston seals, and sudden transmission failures on these years.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. Have a transmission shop check pressures; a rebuild or used transmission is the usual fix.

issues.t: Stalling from a bad mass airflow or crankshaft sensor
issues.sym: The engine dies at a light or while driving, then may restart. Steering and brakes get heavy when it stalls.
issues.why: RepairPal owners report stalling caused by a failing mass airflow sensor or crankshaft position sensor, often past 100,000 miles. NHTSA complaints describe sudden stalling at speed.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the sensors tested. Treat stalling at speed as a safety issue.

issues.t: Won't start because of the anti-theft key system
issues.sym: The engine won't crank or cranks and won't fire, and the security light is on or flashing.
issues.why: This is the most reported problem on RepairPal. The key has a resistor chip, and worn key contacts or broken wiring in the steering column make the car think the wrong key is used.
issues.next: Wait about 10 minutes with the key on, then try again (the system resets). Have the key and column wiring checked; a new key or wiring repair usually fixes it.

issues.sym: Several cranks needed after sitting overnight, worse in cold weather. It may start, die and restart.
issues.why: Owners report long cranking on cold starts. Fuel pressure bleeding off through a leaking regulator or injector is a common cause on this engine.
issues.next: Have a fuel pressure and leak-down test done. If the regulator is leaking, check whether the recall applies.

issues.sym: Oil seeping around the intake, oil smell, or burning oil on the exhaust.
issues.why: RepairPal owners report oil leaks from the intake manifold gaskets, usually above 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the leak traced. The same gasket job fixes both oil and coolant leaks.

issues.t: Low fuel light on with a quarter tank
issues.sym: The low-fuel warning comes on while the gauge shows about a quarter tank.
issues.why: Consumer Guide notes this was fixed by replacing the instrument cluster.
issues.next: Don't rely on the low-fuel light. Have the cluster checked; a used or rebuilt cluster is an option besides new.

issues.t: Overheating and coolant loss at the radiator neck
issues.sym: The engine runs hot and coolant slowly disappears.
issues.why: A rough radiator filler neck lets the cap leak pressure. Consumer Guide says sanding the neck smooth and fitting a new cap fixes it.
issues.next: Rule out intake leaks first, then have the cap and neck checked. Never open the cap while hot.

issues.sym: A click from the steering column when turning the wheel.
issues.why: Consumer Guide notes a loose upper bearing mount in the steering column caused clicking on 1994-1996 cars.
issues.next: Have the column checked and the bearing mount secured.

issues.sym: A soft brake pedal, brake fluid leaks, a gas smell, or fuel dripping under the car.
issues.why: NHTSA complaints describe brake and fuel lines rusting through, especially in road-salt states.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. If the pedal goes soft or you smell fuel, don't drive it. Have the lines inspected, especially along the frame and over the fuel tank.

issues.sym: The steering wheel or pedal shakes when stopping, or the car pulls.
issues.why: Owners report warped rotors and brake vibration in NHTSA complaints.
issues.next: Have rotors measured and replaced if out of spec.

issues.sym: The back of the car sags or bottoms out, and the ride feels harsh.
issues.why: Owners reported the automatic load-leveling system failing, letting the rear sit low.
issues.next: Have the air shocks, lines and compressor checked; regular shocks are another option.

issues.t: Rear seat belts hard to buckle
issues.sym: Rear belts won't latch or the buckle is jammed.
issues.why: Owners reported rear seat belts that are hard or impossible to latch.
issues.next: Have the buckle replaced; it is a safety item.

issues.sym: The horn doesn't work when it's cold.
issues.why: Owners reported the horn failing in cold weather.
issues.next: Have the horn, relay and steering wheel contacts tested.

issues.sym: Wipers quit, chatter across the glass or fly off the arm.
issues.why: Owners reported wiper failures and chattering.
issues.next: Replace blades and have the linkage and motor checked.

issues.sym: The A/C blows warm, or the compressor makes noise.
issues.why: Owners reported A/C compressor failures on this year.
issues.next: Have the system leak-checked before replacing the compressor.
